description: Run N mutating build-buy ops in a single cf round-trip (freesoexperiment-e5e). Each entry dispatches through the same handler the single-op call would use, so the freesoexperiment-fe1 structured verdict (placed|silent-drop|bot-rejected, hints, balance_before/after, etc) carries through per entry. The engine PDU channel is still 1-at-a-time, but the cf round-trip floor is paid once instead of N times — for a 50-op furnished-room build the difference is ~2 min of cf overhead vs ~2.5s. NOT TRANSACTIONAL: the engine has no reverse-op for these commands. Default stop-on-first-failure leaves earlier successful ops in place — they are not undone. continue_on_failure=true opts in to best-effort mode for cases like 'demolish everything, ignore per-entry failures'. Allowed ops (mutating build-buy family only — search-catalog and list-catalog-categories do NOT belong in a batch and are rejected): buy-object, place-from-inventory, move-object, delete-object, send-to-inventory, list-object-for-sale, buy-listed-object, upgrade-object, place-wall, paint-wall, paint-floor, paint-grass, flatten-terrain, raise-terrain, set-roof, change-environment, change-lot-size.

args.name: ops
args.description: Array of op entries, each {op:string (one of the allowed verb names above), ...args for that verb}. The 'op' field is stripped before forwarding; everything else is passed through to the per-op handler. Pre-validated: a single bad op name in the batch rejects the entire batch BEFORE any PDU is sent.

args.name: continue_on_failure
args.description: Default false (stop-on-first-failure: halt and return halted_at + halt_reason on the first non-success verdict). Set true for best-effort mode (run all N ops regardless, return all N verdicts).

common_mistakes: Including a read-only op like search-catalog in a batch — rejected up front; do reads separately before composing the batch.
Expecting transactional rollback on halt — there is none. Earlier successful ops in the batch persist until you undo them yourself.
Mixing 'op' with verb-specific fields under the same key — each entry is an object with 'op' plus all the normal args for that verb. The 'op' field is stripped before forwarding.

Sending more than one batch concurrently to the same body — the per-op handlers serialise on the bot's tick lock, so concurrent batches will interleave entries in unpredictable order. Run one batch at a time per body.
perception_hints: Use batch-build for any multi-op build sequence: room furnishing, demolition, wallpaper passes. The cf-round-trip saving compounds.

Inspect verdicts[i] for per-entry status — placed/deleted means success; silent-drop with hints tells you why a placement failed (tile-occupied, no-budget-debit, etc) the same way the single-op call does.
If halted_at is set, the agent should query-lot-objects to learn the actual placed state and decide whether to retry the remaining entries with adjusted coords.
